name: Efficient Streaming Language Models with Attention Sinks
problem: Streaming applications (multi-round dialogue) need bounded KV memory, but simply keeping the most recent KVs - sliding-window attention - FAILS once the text exceeds the cache size, and popular LLMs cannot generalise past their training length.
mechanism: Identify the ATTENTION SINK phenomenon: attention scores are strongly biased toward the initial tokens even though they are not semantically important, and keeping the KV of just those initial tokens largely recovers sliding-window performance. StreamingLLM therefore keeps a fixed budget of the first few tokens PLUS a rolling recent window, and assigns positions so the window does not drift outside the trained range. Also shows that adding a dedicated placeholder sink token during PRE-TRAINING improves streaming deployment further.
speedup_reported: Paper's own claims (abstract): enables Llama-2, MPT, Falcon and Pythia to do stable and efficient language modelling with up to 4 MILLION tokens and more; in streaming settings it outperforms the sliding-window RECOMPUTATION baseline by up to 22.2x speedup. The baseline is explicit (sliding-window recomputation) and the 22.2x is large because recomputation re-reads the whole context - it is not comparable to a paged-attention engine's number.
